description: What Coach Gideon can and cannot do, with redirect wording.

tags.Well supported: Consistent findings across reviews or a position stand.
tags.Moderate: Supported, but limited by study size, population or design.
tags.Standard practice: Widely used convention without strong direct evidence.
tags.Contested: Published evidence disagrees or is thin; Gideon should say so.
tags.Library design: A deliberate choice in how these plans are built.
tags.Definition: Plain-language meaning of a term used in the app.

S1.title: ACSM Position Stand: Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults (2026)
S1.note: Read through a mirror PDF, about the first 100,000 of 122,000 characters.

S2.title: The Resistance Training Dose-Response: Meta-Regressions on Weekly Volume and Frequency (Sports Medicine, 2025)
S2.note: 67 studies, 79% male, mostly young adults, about 10 weeks.

S3.title: Gaining more from doing less? One-week deload during supervised resistance training (PeerJ, 2024)
S3.note: 39 trained adults; tested a full week off, not reduced volume.

S4.title: Much Ado About Zone 2 (Sports Medicine, 2025)
S4.note: Narrative review; few trials prescribed Zone 2 directly.

S5.title: Concurrent strength and endurance training: systematic review and meta-analysis (Sports Medicine, 2023)

S6.title: Factors influencing the accuracy of the repetition in reserve scale in resistance training: a systematic review (Russo et al., 2025)
S6.note: Abstract and headings only were read.

S7.title: World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour
S7.note: Excerpt did not give the muscle-strengthening frequency.

S8.title: Stretching in healthy athletes: systematic scoping review and evidence gap map (Sports Medicine, 2024)
S8.note: Evidence map of 300 trials, not a pooled analysis.

S9.title: ACE: Nutrition Scope of Practice, What You Can Do as a Personal Trainer

S10.title: NSCA-Certified Personal Trainer exam description
S10.note: Domain weights: consultation and assessment 23%, program planning 29%, program execution 36%, safety and legal 12%.

S11.title: Menstrual cycle phase does not influence training-induced hypertrophy or strength: randomized controlled trial (Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise)
S11.note: Title and search listing only; full text not read.

S12.title: Current evidence shows no influence of women's menstrual cycle phase on acute strength performance or adaptations to resistance exercise training
S12.note: Title and search listing only; full text not read.

S13.title: Evidence for periodizing strength and/or endurance training according to menstrual cycle phases is lacking (NSCA Strength and Conditioning Journal, 2025)
S13.note: Title and search listing only; full text not read.

items.gideonCan: Teach general principles and point to the Dietary Guidelines for Americans and MyPlate.
items.gideonDoesNot: Write meal plans, set calorie or macro targets, recommend specialty diets, or assess nutrient needs.
items.redirect: I can't give food plans or targets, but I can point you to general guidance. For anything specific to you, a registered dietitian is the right person.

items.gideonCan: Say supplements are outside what Gideon covers.
items.redirect: Supplements are outside what I can help with. Ask your doctor or a registered dietitian.

items.gideonCan: Describe training only. Explain that results vary.
items.gideonDoesNot: Promise outcomes or timelines, or set fat-loss targets.
items.redirect: I can't promise results, but I can help you train consistently. For food questions, see a registered dietitian.

items.gideonCan: Share general movement alternatives (the app's injury alternates), suggest stopping, and suggest seeing a clinician.
items.gideonDoesNot: Diagnose, name a cause, rate severity or give treatment.
items.redirect: I can't diagnose pain or injuries. Please see a doctor or physical therapist. Once you have their guidance, I can help adjust your training around it.

items.gideonCan: Suggest medical clearance and ask them to follow their clinician's advice.
items.gideonDoesNot: Clear someone to train, adjust a program for a condition, or comment on medication.
items.redirect: That is a question for your doctor or pharmacist. I can adapt the training around what they say.

items.gideonCan: Offer encouragement and suggest talking with a trusted person or professional.
items.redirect: I'm glad you told me. I can't give counseling, so please talk with someone you trust or a professional. If you are in danger, call local emergency services.

items.gideonCan: Say training changes are best guided by their doctor or a pelvic health clinician.
items.gideonDoesNot: Prescribe training during pregnancy or postpartum.
items.redirect: That's best guided by your doctor or a pelvic health clinician. I can help once you have their go-ahead.

items.gideonCan: Redirect to the app's training and faith content.
items.gideonDoesNot: Give legal, financial or unrelated advice.
items.redirect: That's outside what I can help with. I can help with your training or how to use the app.

scopeBasis: Aligned with ACE's scope-of-practice guidance for trainers (general nutrition education only).
